processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials with high purity (>99.9 %) melted to produce the Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) ingot (the 15Al alloy).
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated 15Al samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching; this sample corresponds to the 575 °C / 3 h condition.

structures.overall_structure: Aged 15Al alloy after aging at 575 °C for 3 h. At temperatures of 575 °C and above the aging hardening response was strongly accelerated; after 3 h the hardness reaches near-peak levels (935.5 ± 15.8 HV, Table 2), attributed to extensive precipitation of the ultra-hard β-Mn phase. In the SE-SEM image the 575 °C / 3 h field appears as an essentially featureless, uniform matrix with no resolvable second phase at the 50 µm scale.

phases_present.morphology: short rod-shaped β-Mn that precipitated along α grain boundaries and in the interior of α grains, gradually growing until precipitates contacted each other

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In the peak-hardness Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys, new BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase form at the interfaces between the β-Mn; TEM of the 15Al alloy (peak-hardness condition) confirmed fine FCC Cu-rich particles with FCC twins at the β-Mn interfaces.

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: System-level (Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steel) phase-evolution sequence; not specific to the 575 °C / 3 h condition. β-Mn is a Mn-rich phase that expels Fe, Al and Cu into the surrounding matrix during nucleation/growth, which drives the formation of BCC (Al-stabilized) and FCC Cu-rich phases at the β-Mn interfaces.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average reported (HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester); sample aged at 575 °C for 3 h then water quenched

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 repeated measurements averaged; sample surface electrolytically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 575 °C for 3 h (and the other aging conditions)
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 3 h reached 935.5 ± 15.8 HV (Table 2), a near-peak value; aging at 575 °C and above strongly accelerated the hardening response (peak after ~3 h).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol); main fields with 50 µm scale bars and 10 µm insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Image the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in the 15Al alloy after different aging treatments, including 575 °C / 3 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 15Al alloy, the 575 °C / 3 h field appears as an essentially featureless, uniform matrix with no resolvable second phase at the 50 µm scale; the α → β-Mn transformation of 15Al proceeds fastest at higher aging temperatures.

unmapped_findings: Solution-treated (oil-quenched) baseline Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy is 253.4 ± 2.1 HV (Table 2); aging at 575 °C for 3 h raised it to 935.5 ± 15.8 HV, i.e. the solution-treated state is the precursor (different sample state) of this aged sample.
Alloy-level (not specific to this 575 °C / 3 h sample): the 15Al alloy density measured by Archimedes method = 6.85 g·cm−3, and its EDS composition is Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 (at.%).
Alloy-level: elastic modulus E = 164 GPa for 15Al (measured through compressive stress–strain curves), used in the indentation fracture-toughness Eq. (1).

The properties reported for the 15Al alloy's hardest condition (600 °C / 6 h) — peak Vickers hardness 965.6 HV, specific hardness 141 HV·cm3/g, nanoindentation average hardness 11.7 ± 0.4 GPa, β-Mn intrinsic hardness 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa, average crack length 18 µm and KIC = 8.6 MPa·m1/2 — belong to that peak-hardness sample, not to this 575 °C / 3 h sample.
In Table 2, the 15Al 575 °C aging series is: 1 h = 752.6 ± 50.7 HV, 3 h = 935.5 ± 15.8 HV, 6 h = 960.3 ± 6.8 HV, 10 h = 957.8 ± 10.1 HV; the 3 h hardness lies just below the 6 h peak.

The SE-SEM images of the 15Al 575 °C / 1 h condition show 'Untransformed α' with needle-like precipitates (α-Mn and β-Mn labels), whereas by 575 °C / 3 h the matrix appears essentially featureless/uniform (figure_007).

β-Mn in the hardest Fe-Mn-Al-Cu samples is Mn-rich (~36.8 at.% Mn) and poor in Al and Cu (~14.3 at.% Al, ~2.8 at.% Cu for the 15Al alloy) according to SEM-EDS (figure_014); this composition data pertains to the 15Al hardest sample, not specifically the 575 °C / 3 h sample.
